companyIntro.name: Summit Advisory
companyIntro.mission: Help leadership teams make better decisions with structured thinking and evidence.
companyIntro.culture: Answer first, then prove it. Every slide earns its place and every number has a source.

projectBackground.name: Market Entry Strategy — Home Energy App
projectBackground.context: Norden is considering a home-energy app for 2 million households. The CEO wants an answer, not a report.

manager.name: Alexandra Pryce
manager.note: Answer first. If I need to read three pages to find your recommendation, you've already lost the room.

assignment.title: Recommend whether and how to enter
assignment.brief: Size the market, quantify savings, rank options in Excel and write the executive summary.

documents.name: Market Data
documents.note: 2,000,000 target households; 15% expected adoption; €120 annual revenue per user.

documents.name: Options Long-List
documents.note: Three entry options scored on impact, feasibility and risk.

tasks.title: Structuring
tasks.prompt: Which structure is MECE for 'why did profit fall'?
options: A list of ideas in random order
Revenue decline versus cost increase, then break each down
tasks.reasoning: Mutually exclusive, collectively exhaustive structures avoid gaps and overlap.
tasks.mistake: Unstructured lists miss causes and double count.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Market Size
tasks.prompt: 2,000,000 households x 15% adoption x €120 per year. What is the annual market size (€)?
tasks.reasoning: Top-down sizing multiplies population, adoption and price.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Cost Savings
tasks.prompt: Costs are €46M and a 3% reduction is targeted. What is the saving (€)?
tasks.reasoning: Savings apply to the cost base, not revenue.
tasks.mistake: Applying 3% to revenue overstates the saving.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Hypothesis-Driven Approach
tasks.prompt: Select steps of a hypothesis-driven approach.
options: Collect all data first before thinking
Identify the analyses that would prove or disprove it
Update the hypothesis as evidence arrives
State an initial answer to test
tasks.reasoning: Starting with a hypothesis focuses work.
tasks.tip: Be willing to be wrong early.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Options Scoring (Excel)
tasks.prompt: Weighted score in column E = B x 0.5 + C x 0.3 + D x 0.2 for each option. Upload for checking.
tasks.reasoning: Weighted scoring makes trade-offs explicit and debatable.
tasks.mistake: Scoring first and then choosing weights fixes the result.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Executive Summary
tasks.prompt: Write a 3-5 sentence answer-first summary for the CEO.
tasks.modelAnswer: We recommend entering through a partnership with a utility. The market is about €36M a year (2M households, 15% adoption, €120 each) and the partnership option scores highest at 7.1 against 6.6 for building or acquiring. It lowers risk and speeds launch, and the cost programme adds €1.38M of profit to help fund it. The decision needed today is approval to open partner talks; the main risk is partner dependence, which we propose to limit with a two-year review clause.
tasks.reasoning: A good executive summary states the recommendation first, then the 2-3 numbers that justify it and the decision required.
tasks.mistake: Burying the answer wastes the executive's attention.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

caseStudy.title: Case Study: The 120-Page Report
caseStudy.background: A consulting team delivered a 120-page report with the recommendation on page 97. The client missed the market window while debating the analysis.
questions: How do you balance rigour and speed?
caseStudy.solution: Summit adopted the pyramid principle for all deliverables: answer, key arguments, then evidence.
